description: Exact RGBs in F3's final 16-color quantized palette eligible for palette-variant remapping. Only the top and trousers families are listed — skin (light, freckled) and hair (auburn ponytail) are never remapped, matching the roster-integration structural decision (#2) and beingPalette.ts's existing remap-table shape (garment-only exact-RGB swap).

top.note: Dominant sage fill, verified clean via a strap-free back-view torso patch and cross-checked against hair, boot, and strap/bag samples.
Fold/sleeve shading, same clean back-view patch.

trousers.note: Dominant cream fill, verified on both legs (front rows 35-37) with zero contamination.

Leg-fold shading, same clean rows. Note: (129,72,32), the crotch-seam shadow one row below this patch, was excluded — it doubles as the boot's main color (confirmed by a dedicated boot-only sample), not a trousers tone.

excludedFromRemap.note: Verified by direct sampling: (138,50,18) reads as the dominant tone in a dedicated hip-bag sample AND independently appears in a pure back-view hair-mass sample (7 of 40 px) — a multi-role hair/strap color, excluded. (129,72,32) is the boot's main color (5/7 in a boot-only sample) but also fills the trousers' crotch-seam shadow one row below the clean trousers patch — excluded despite sitting inside the leg silhouette. (201,100,46) is the rare, dedicated lip/mouth tone (49 px total, appears nowhere else) — a facial-feature color, not garment.

suggestedVariant.name: violet-grey
suggestedVariant.note: One example remap into the world's muted garment families (BEING_PALETTE_VARIANTS in beingPalette.ts: slate-blue / violet-grey / moss / ochre / bone) — F1 used slate-blue, F2 used moss, so this proposes violet-grey for variety. Values preserve F3's own top/trousers luminance spacing. Re-validate visually against the actual atlas render before locking in for R3.
